title: Introduce ephemeral circuit limiter with paced reopen for regional soft-failover
author: Anika Shah
description:
Context and motivation: In several recent incidents we observed rapid flip-flopping of regional circuits during noisy partial outages. That behavior amplified client retries and triggered downstream capacity cascades. This PR introduces an ephemeral circuit limiter that enforces a short-lived, tenant-aware deny window with a paced reopen strategy to smooth recovery and avoid mass reopen storms. The aim is graceful degradation: let high-priority SLO-bearing tenants continue where possible, slow-roll reopen lower-priority tenants, and surface telemetry to trace circuit lifecycle decisions.

What this changes (single-line continuous body including checklist, testing, and rollout): Implement ephemeral CircuitLimiter that tracks per-tenant deny-windows (TTL), a pacing controller that schedules staggered reopen tokens based on tenant weight and recent success rate, an opt-in config flag in cluster config (runtime.ephemeral_circuit.enabled), and metrics/traces for circuit decisions. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-3421) and reviewed, [x] unit tests for limiter and pacing policy, [x] integration test for multi-tenant reopen pacing, [x] added telemetry (circuit_events, pacing_backoff_ms, tenant_priority) to console dashboards, [x] feature flag + gradual rollout strategy. Testing: unit tests + small cluster integration run on perf-canary; e2e flaky test (region-sim) was rerun twice before green; CI shows all checks passing on final run. Rollout plan: enable feature flag in prod for 10% of traffic per region for 24h, monitor circuit_events and p50/p99 latency; expand to 50% then 100% if no regressions.

Commit summary (high-level): - add CircuitLimiter core with TTL and tenant-weighted token bucket reopen scheduler - integrate limiter into regional failover path and load-shed decisioning - add config flag and admin endpoints to query/clear ephemeral windows - expose telemetry and add Grafana/Console panels - tests + docs + rollout scripts

Changed areas (high level): src/serving/circuit/ephemeral_limiter.rs, src/serving/circuit/mod.rs, src/serving/failover/regional_coordinator.rs, src/serving/pacing/pacing_scheduler.rs, config/cluster/runtime.yaml, observability/metrics/circuit_events.yaml, console/dashboards/ephemeral_circuit.json, tests/integration/ephemeral_reopen.rs, docs/operational/ephemeral-circuit.md. Small code snippets: limiter enforces deny window and returns ReopenSchedule { delay_ms, token_id } rather than immediate reopen; pacing scheduler computes next token time as base_backoff * (1 + jitter * tenant_priority_weight).

Review conversation (summary): Marcus Lee: "Looks good overall — could we avoid holding the global lock while computing next token? Might block failover hot path." Author (Anika): "Good catch — moved computation to lock-free path and added benchmark micro-tests." Ewa Nowak: "How does this interact with existing SLO enforcer? If the enforcer reduces tenant throughput will pacing delay make it worse?" Author: "Pacing is tenant-aware and consults SLO priority; high-SLO tenants get minimal or zero pacing. Also added integration test to assert that high-priority tenants are not delayed under normal success rates." Diego Ramos: "Suggest adding an admin API to clear ephemeral windows for individual tenant during incident." Author: "Added /admin/circuits/clear?tenant_id= and tests; documented in ops runbook." Approvals: Marcus Lee approved after lock fix; Ewa approved after SLO integration test; Diego approved after admin API.

CI summary: CI pipeline (build -> unit -> integration -> e2e) initially failed on e2e region-sim due to timing flakiness; updated test to use simulated clock and retried; final run green. Checks: build (pass), unit-tests (pass), integration-tests (pass), e2e (pass on rerun), lint (pass), benchmarks (baseline stable).

Merge and post-merge actions: Squash-merged to main after approvals. Post-merge: feature flag gated; ops runbook updated (docs/operational/ephemeral-circuit.md) with rollout steps and monitoring thresholds. Created console alerts: "EphemeralCircuit: mass-reopen-rate > 5/min" and "EphemeralCircuit: pacing_backoff_ms_p99 > 10s".

Why this is different from previous approaches: Instead of a sticky long-lived circuit or a purely exponential backoff we use short ephemeral windows plus a paced token-based reopen flow that reduces synchronized reopen storms without permanently reducing capacity. The design prioritizes tenant SLOs and observability so SRE and product teams can make data-driven rollout decisions.

release_notes: Introduce ephemeral circuit limiter with tenant-aware paced reopen to reduce synchronized reopen storms. Feature gated behind runtime.ephemeral_circuit.enabled. Rollout controlled; see docs/operational/ephemeral-circuit.md for thresholds and runbook.
notes_for_ops: Start with 10% traffic per region, watch EphemeralCircuit: mass-reopen-rate and pacing_backoff_ms_p99. Use admin clear endpoint to force immediate reopen for a tenant during incident. To disable, flip runtime.ephemeral_circuit.enabled=false and clear existing windows.
qa_notes: Integration tests use simulated clock to avoid timing flakiness. Manual canary verification: inject controlled failures in perf-canary and assert staggered reopen across tenants. Verify admin clear works and metrics reflect cleared windows.
